title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
question: Given an integer array sorted in ascending order that has been rotated at an unknown pivot, how would you search for a target value in O(log N) time?

rubric.name: problem_clarification
rubric.description: Clarifies duplicate element existence, array boundaries, and return value for missing targets.

rubric.name: algorithmic_reasoning
rubric.description: Identifies that one half of array must remain strictly sorted at any midpoint and uses this property to prune search space.

rubric.name: time_space_complexity
rubric.description: Explains why target search takes O(log N) time and O(1) space iteratively.

rubric.name: edge_case_handling
rubric.description: Handles single-element array, array rotated 0 times, and duplicates (if mentioned).

rubric.name: communication_clarity
rubric.description: Walks through binary search boundary adjustments step-by-step.

expected_signals: Checks whether left half `nums[low] <= nums[mid]` is sorted before determining target bounds
Derives correct index updates for `low` and `high`
red_flags: Proposes O(N) linear search without recognizing binary search potential
Fails to handle pivot boundary condition correctly
Ignores integer overflow when calculating midpoint in certain languages
follow_up_prompts: How does the time complexity change if the array contains duplicate values?
How would you find the pivot index itself (the minimum element) in O(log N) time?
